column1: # Cross-module fn value in a higher-order word's CLOSURE slot
# (design/FUNCTION-VALUE-SCOPE.0.md §12.3).
# A function value resolves its free words in the module that DEFINED it. The
# interpreter now does this at every seam; the compiler cannot yet, because it
# lowers a higher-order word's fn operand to a closure unit compiled against
# the CALLING module. Compiling this body against the caller silently baked the
# caller's `lim` (100) and returned [] where the interpreter returns [3 4] — a
# compile != interpret miscompile, check-clean. compiler/go/callable_words.go's
# foreignFnHome therefore DECLINES the lowering, and `filter` islands.
# GRADUATED 2026-08-27 (Stage 3) into lang/spec/module-fnvalue-boundary.tsv §4,
# where the rest of that section always lived. The closure lowering now
# compiles a foreign body against its DEFINING registry with the CALLER's
# CheckState shared onto it, so the island is gone and `filter A.big` compiles
# natively. The paragraphs above are kept as the record of what the island was
# and why it was correct while it stood.
# ADR-016 / NUR077 §5 Hole 1 (2026-08-21): `apply` on a fn whose ONLY
#   signatures are 0-arg now applies it at the apply site itself, so
#   origin no longer decides at arity 0 (`z/v apply` and `f/v apply`
#   both answer 42). The COMPILED lane cannot model it: the check
#   engine re-steps the fn value, and execFnDefLiteral's data gate —
#   which must stay, since it is what parks `f/v` and holds a lambda
#   in a container — leaves an anonymous 0-arg value inert, so the
#   program would const-fold to the FUNCTION. apply's check-mode model
#   declines instead and the interpreter fallback answers. Compiling the
#   shape natively is the follow-up.
def f ([] => [42])  f/v apply
column3: a 0-arg LAMBDA handed to apply — interpreter-correct, compile declined (ledgered)
